iterations.changes: Added an ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English output-language section to all five skills (spring_clean, rebug, audit, address-pr-comments, pr-review). Iterated once inside the iteration: v1 measurably shed file:line citations, so v2 adds a 'Do not lose information' rule — STE limits sentence length, not the number of sentences or facts; keep every number, citation, and downstream effect; the six-sentence cap is per paragraph, so use more paragraphs or a vertical list.

arms.ste2: STE section v1 + 'Do not lose information'

iterations.notes: STE conformance improved on every skill with no structural regression: template_pass_rate stayed 1.0 in all arms, recall stayed 1.0, and address-pr-comments kept 100% verdict accuracy with both false-positive traps caught. The one real regression in v1 was information loss — citations per finding roughly halved on spring_clean (4.28 -> 1.94) and rebug (4.7 -> 1.87), because a sentence-length budget invites dropping the subordinate clause that carried a quantity or an extra location. v2 fixes it: citations recover to 3.42 and quantities rise above baseline (1.78 -> 4.05), while conformance holds or improves. Side benefit: the 'keep the section titles and field names exactly as they are' rule hardened template fidelity — the base arm drifted to [CRITICAL] casing and numbered '### Issue 3:' headings, the STE arms did not. Two eval-asset defects found and recorded in iteration-4/ground_truth_eventbus.json corrections: MemoryStorage is mislabelled clean, and the RetryMiddleware clean label needs to name with_retry() rather than the class.
iterations.caveats: One sample per arm, so differences under roughly 10 percent are inside run-to-run variance. Recall saturates at 1.0 because test-repo sources carry greppable '# BUG [CATEGORY]:' annotations, so recall cannot detect a small loss of discovery — a blind copy is the next harness fix. pr-review is confounded: its base arm came from c1019cd, which predates both the STE section and the uncommitted 'Simplicity & economy' taxonomy, so its base-vs-ste delta mixes two changes. That work is committed separately, immediately before this iteration, so the next pr-review measurement has a clean baseline.

iterations.changes: New skill perform-like-jeff-dean: performance audit distilled from Abseil's Performance Hints. Hot/cold classification before flagging, back-of-envelope Estimate field anchored in the latency-numbers table, 6-category taxonomy, and a P1-P4 priority matrix (impact x effort) so quick wins rank first; cold-code inefficiencies become one-line notes. New eval assets: test-repo/perfburn (18 planted issues, 6 FP traps, no in-source BUG annotations) and priority_score.py (pairwise order accuracy, label accuracy, section-aware recall, trap hits on unmatched findings only). 10 ground-truth labels corrected after arithmetic review, recorded in the corrections array. v2 (one ralph-wiggum cycle later): sweep cold files with the same patterns (hits become Cold-Code Notes) and record every dismissed candidate in Not Found with the dismissing number. v3: fan out read-only exploration subagents on large repositories (split by subsystem, candidates not findings, central verification); inert on small repos by design.

iterations.notes: The stub baseline found issues but produced no parseable template, so its structure and priority metrics are zero/absent by construction. The v1 report's estimates exposed 10 miscalibrated ground-truth labels (e.g. re.compile is cached by CPython; SELECT * over a 432M-row day is High, not Medium; the 'startup-only' index build actually runs per CLI query invocation and has no reader). All 6 FP traps handled correctly: cold inefficiencies went to Cold-Code Notes, the lru_cache and batched-flush traps were explicitly dismissed or praised. v2 verdict: recall_total 1.0 (PB-ALGO-3 caught), precision and STE up, cost down 16%. citations_per_finding dropped 34% on perfburn but rose 42% on eventbus under the same skill text; inspection showed de-duplication of repeated chain/README citations with unique files cited unchanged - judged variance plus compression of redundancy, not information loss. All stop-rule targets met at v2; loop stopped per rule (a). v3 verdict: the fan-out text is inert on the small targets (the model never attempted subagents; denial patterns identical to v2), so the two-sample run checked prompt dilution only. v3 sample regressed on ordering/labels, the v3-b duplicate swung back above every gate (precision 1.0, traps 0, citations 10.21) - judged run variance, committed. Ordering spread across all versions is 0.78-0.95; treating single-sample ordering deltas as signal is a mistake this eval should stop making (raise samples or plant wider tier gaps). The fan-out behavior itself needs the planned large target (test-repo/bazaar).
iterations.caveats: Single sample per arm (<10% deltas are noise). The only true miss is PB-ALGO-3 (sorted() for top-10 in the daily reportgen). Label-accuracy denominators are matched ranked findings only.

iterations.changes: New test surface, no skill change: test-repo/bazaar, a 250-file / 11.3k-LOC async marketplace monorepo authored by 7 parallel writer agents (31 planted issues after adjudication, 10 traps, 8 clean items, 4 cross-subsystem issues, 3 client-server N+1s, 2 zero-plant restraint subsystems, no in-source annotations). Iteration-7 harness adds a disallowed-tools override to run_skill.sh, batch-bazaar.sh (solo/fanout/guard), and coverage_score.py (subsystem coverage, restraint, cross-subsystem synthesis, P4 discipline).

arms.adjudicate: fanout tools vs draft GT (in-sample after corrections)

iterations.notes: The differential answers the iteration-6 open question: on a repo above the skill's fan-out threshold, parallel exploration subagents match or beat the solo sweep on every quality gate (precision 1.0 vs 0.885, ordering 0.884 vs 0.862, coverage and cross-subsystem synthesis perfect in both) at 43% of the cost, 22% of the tokens, and 75% of the wall time - the solo arm burned 15.3M tokens dragging the whole repo through one context. Adjudication against the draft GT produced 8 corrections: 3 organic writer-agent defects adopted as planted issues (serial webhook dispatch P2 among them), all 3 designed P4s demoted because the written code offered Small fixes, one matcher-blur false match fixed by rewording. The guard run stayed within iteration-6 bands.
iterations.caveats: Single sample per arm. The adjudicate arm is in-sample by construction. p4 metrics are vacuous until a true P4 plant survives adjudication. Solo's 3 unmatched P3-grade extras await review.

iterations.changes: Subtraction, 306 -> 258 lines. Replaced the generic Correctness/Security/Error handling/Performance/Best practices/Observability/Maintainability checklists with one short 'Implementation categories' block that names only the checks reviewers skip. Replaced the 18-bullet Guidelines section (16 bullets restated earlier phases) with 5 rules. 'Issues Not Found' is now one line plus exceptions. Added: a runtime finding must construct the concrete failure (input or state -> wrong result) or go to Open Questions; scale the report to the PR; defects the PR did not introduce are not findings against it.
iterations.notes: First ground-truth eval for pr-review. On the planted PR both pr-review arms find all 17 planted issues with 0 trap hits and 0 review-comment reads; cost, time and length are unchanged within noise. On the clean PR the subtraction is a clear gain over three samples per arm: findings 1.67 -> 0 (the base arm reported older, out-of-scope defects as Low findings), report length -51%, wall time -45%, cost -32%. The native /code-review matches pr-review on implementation recall (1.0) at about one fifth of the cost and one sixth of the time, finds 61% of design-tier issues (it misses the mock-only tests, the weakened test, and the description mismatches), gives no severity, and reported 6 findings on the clean PR.
iterations.caveats: Recall is saturated, so this iteration cannot show that the removed checklists cost nothing on harder PRs. Small samples.

targets: test-repo/parcelpost PR #3 (bulk: 13 planted issues that need cross-file context, 3 traps)
iterations.changes: Test surface only: PR #3 with cross-file bugs and architectural defects.
iterations.notes: The subtle tier did not separate the arms. Both pr-review versions found all 13 planted issues in both samples, with 0 trap hits and 0 review-comment reads; the matches were checked by hand (the two F5 trap candidates are the phrase 'leaks 2 labels', not the trap claim). The native /code-review again found every implementation bug (7 of 7) at about a fifth of the cost; it missed the description mismatch and the weak rollback test in both samples, and two architectural findings in one sample. Conclusion: at +150 lines in a 15-file repo the reviewer reads every relevant file, so cross-file subtlety is not hard for this model. Difficulty has to come from scale (a PR whose callers and precedents do not fit in one read, such as a PR into test-repo/bazaar) or from domain rules that are not written in the repo.
